title: Reverse an Array In Place
statement:
You are given an array of `n` integers. Reverse the array **in place**: rearrange its elements so that the first element becomes the last, the second becomes the second-to-last, and so on, using only a constant amount of extra memory (do not build a second array of size `n`).

Print the array after it has been reversed.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Print the reversed array as `n` space-separated integers on one line.

examples.explanation: Element 0 swaps with element 4, and element 1 swaps with element 3. The middle element stays where it is.
Swap positions 0 and 3, then positions 1 and 2. Equal values are still moved like any others.
A single element is its own reverse.

hints: Which pairs of positions need to exchange their values? Position i pairs with position n - 1 - i.
Use two pointers, one at each end, swap, and move them toward each other.
Stop when the pointers meet or cross; each pair must be swapped only once, otherwise you undo your work.
